instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Hidden Power
cards.instruction: Act publicly modest while making choices as though you control the outcome.

cards.title: How Much Do You Know?
cards.instruction: Probe for what others know while revealing as little as possible.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm only collecting the party photos. Before I send the album, what have you heard about the cake?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It went over the balcony. Was that before you left?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll leave the balcony page blank for now. Who gave you the timing?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Nobody. Your brother says there's a video.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Have you watched it? If not, I'll use a photograph of the intact cake. We can leave my brother's version out of the album.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm just filling in the lost-key book. What did the manager actually say? I'll decide whether to call maintenance once that's clear.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They might be in the drain. You locked up, didn't you?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Is she asking everyone that, or just me? No point having the drain opened on a guess.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Just you. Someone saw you outside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Did they see what I was doing, or only where I was? I'll leave maintenance out of it until we have something more useful than 'outside'.

cards.title: Join Me
cards.instruction: Recruit someone into a secret plan.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd only be peeling apples. Could you keep Mum in the kitchen for twenty minutes while I hide her birthday cake?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only if you stop telling her I'm the one who plans these things.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll do the explaining afterwards. Ask her for the pastry lesson; I'll bring the cake in once she's got flour on her hands.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She'll make me bake a whole pie.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll have the apples sliced before you start. Ask for the lattice top; she can teach you that while I finish hiding the cake.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm only keeping the calendar tidy. I've left seven free for Denise's surprise party; could you get her out while I decorate?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I spent the last one washing glasses.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put my name down for washing. I'll move our team catch-up to tomorrow, so you've got time to take her for coffee.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She won't leave before I finish her spreadsheet.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Send it to me; I'll finish it before seven. You take her out when I send it back, and tell her you're exhausted from doing it all yourself.

cards.title: You First
cards.instruction: Coax someone else into breaking a rule before you do.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm only here to carry your flowers. We'll do the rooftop photograph first; try that staff-only door and I'll follow you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm the bride. They'll notice me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They'll forgive the dress. I'll keep the photographer here until you've had a first look at the roof.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then carry my train.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Gladly. I'll hold the end from this side of the door. You go through first; if nobody objects, I'll bring the rest of your dress and follow you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm only carrying the shopping, but I'm not taking home another sour bunch. Try one of these before we buy them.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The sign says no tasting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just one. I'll keep the bunch out of our basket until you tell me it's sweet; then I'll try the next.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. I'll hold it out like samples. You take the first one; if the assistant lets that pass, I'll have mine before we pay.

cards.title: Recognize Me
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge your importance, expertise, or authority.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm only looking after the scissors. Before I hand them over for the bridge opening, who are you thanking?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The whole town.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I'll keep the ribbon intact while you mention who stopped the bridge leaning into the river.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You did. We thanked the engineers in the programme.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No need for another programme. Just say my name into the microphone, and I'll put the scissors straight into your hand.

cards.title: Choose Me
cards.instruction: Make yourself the choice over another person, plan, or obligation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I don't need a fuss for my birthday. Just come here instead of the concert; I've made your favourite cake and put dinner back for you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've already bought two tickets.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bring your friend. I'll feed you both and pay for the tickets; nobody needs to make a speech.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She only agreed because I promised her dancing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll clear the living room before you arrive. You two choose the music; I'll keep the first slow dance for us.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd be happy just carrying the camera. Take me instead of Martin and I'll handle all the French updates from the expedition.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're crossing a desert, not interviewing people.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your sponsor's French. I'll send them a picture and caption every evening, before anyone posts the day's photographs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They want their logo in every picture.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll put it on the water flask and use that in the foreground. Martin likes untouched wilderness; I'll make sure the sponsor sees what they've paid for.
